As somebody who has kept rats as pets for about 10 years it always surprised me so many people find them so repulsive, and just wondered why?
Why do people find pet rats so repulsive?

Because historically rats are considered carriers of pestilence and disease. They were blamed on the black plague (even though that was fleas), and we have various traps to keep them and their more-common cousins, mice, out of our homes to avoid structural damage and bacteria from urine and feces. It should be noted that mice and rats are also commonly lumped together, even though they aren't the same things. Because having a rodent infested home is considered the worst thing ever, people would wonder why one would choose to keep such a seemingly awful thing voluntarily.

It should be noted that I don't think rats are repulsive, nor mice--if anything, the only thing that bugs me, as with all small rodent like creatures, is that I'm afraid they might bite me while I'm handling them. And, of course, you may take all of these points and try to say "well that's not true because x y z", but of course this isn't a question about what you think, it's why other people think it, and that's why.

*Humans in general also seem to have a mild revulsion to all things smaller than a miniature dog breed in general--rodents, insects, arachnids, snakes, wild fish, etc. That might just be a human thing, though.
